multipleChoice.question: Why does the stranger come to the spring at the beginning of Chapter 7?
options: He wants to learn about Jesus
He is very thirsty, he and his donkey
He is looking for James
He wants to sit in the shade
multipleChoice.explanation: The stranger says: I am very thirsty, I and my donkey. Can you give us water to drink?

multipleChoice.question: Who draws water and gives it to the thirsty stranger?
options: James
The donkey
Salome
A farmer passing by
multipleChoice.explanation: Salome draws water and gives it to the thirsty stranger. She then also gives water to the donkey.

multipleChoice.question: How does James know the things he teaches about Jesus?
options: From books
From the shepherd in the field
Through the Holy Spirit
From the farmers in the fields
multipleChoice.explanation: James says: I know these things through the Holy Spirit. The one who believes in Jesus receives the Holy Spirit.

multipleChoice.question: What does Salome say James has been telling her about Jesus?
options: That Jesus is the good farmer
That Jesus is the Son of God, the Christ
That Jesus is a great teacher only
That Jesus is the God of Abraham alone
multipleChoice.explanation: Salome says: James is speaking to me about Jesus, who is the Son of God, the Christ.

multipleChoice.question: What does the stranger know about God at the start of the conversation?
options: He knows Jesus well
He knows the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob but not Jesus
He knows nothing about God
He knows the Holy Spirit
multipleChoice.explanation: The stranger says he knows the God who made heaven and earth, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, but he does not know Jesus.

multipleChoice.question: Who is James say is the Father of Jesus?
options: Abraham
The shepherd
The God who makes heaven and earth
The stranger
multipleChoice.explanation: James says: the God who makes heaven and earth is the Father of Jesus.

multipleChoice.question: What title does James give to Jesus when comparing him to the water Salome gives the stranger?
options: The bread of the earth
The bread of life, who gives the water of life
The living spring
The one descending into the field
multipleChoice.explanation: James says Jesus is the bread of life, descending from heaven, who gives the water of life to the thirsty soul.

multipleChoice.question: What does Salome say about Jesus and the vine?
options: Jesus plants the vine in the field
Jesus is the true vine and we are the branches
The vine guards the sheep
The branches give water like the spring
multipleChoice.explanation: Salome says: James tells me that Jesus is the true vine and we are the branches. The one who remains in Jesus bears much fruit.

multipleChoice.question: According to James, who cannot receive the Holy Spirit?
options: Those who are too young
Those who do not believe
Women who seek God
Those who thirst for water
multipleChoice.explanation: James confirms: the one who does not believe does not receive the Spirit. The world cannot receive it because it neither sees nor knows it.

multipleChoice.question: According to the story, who gives the Paraclete to believers?
options: James
The Father, through his love for the Son
The stranger
The world
multipleChoice.explanation: Jesus asks the Father, and the Father who loves the Son gives us another Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, to abide with us forever.

multipleChoice.question: How long does the Holy Spirit abide with believers?
options: Only while they are at the spring
For one generation
Forever, into the age
Until the sun sets
multipleChoice.explanation: The Father gives the Spirit so that it may abide with us forever, into the age.

multipleChoice.question: What does the Holy Spirit do for the believer, according to James?
options: It gives money and strength
It teaches all things and bears witness about Jesus
It guards the sheep
It draws water from the spring
multipleChoice.explanation: The Holy Spirit teaches the believer all things and bears witness about Jesus in the believing heart.

multipleChoice.question: What does James say about a woman who seeks God?
options: She cannot receive the Spirit
She receives the Spirit just as a man does
She must ask a man to receive it for her
She must first come to the spring
multipleChoice.explanation: The woman who seeks God receives the Spirit just as the man does.

multipleChoice.question: What does the stranger say after James explains the work of the Holy Spirit?
options: He says he already has the Spirit
He says he wants to hear more about this Spirit
He says he does not believe any of it
He says the Spirit is like water
multipleChoice.explanation: The stranger is silent and marvels, then rises and says: I want to hear more about this Spirit. What does it do in the believing person?

multipleChoice.question: What does James say the Paraclete does for a person who forgets the words of Jesus?
options: It punishes them
It teaches them again and brings the words back to their heart
It removes them from the flock
It replaces them with a hired hand
multipleChoice.explanation: James teaches that the person who does not remember the words of Jesus — the Spirit teaches again and brings the words into his heart.

trueFalse.statement: The stranger and his donkey arrive at the spring and are very thirsty.
trueFalse.explanation: The stranger says: I am very thirsty, I and my donkey. Can you give us water to drink?

trueFalse.statement: James draws water and gives it to the stranger.
trueFalse.explanation: It is Salome who draws the water and gives it to the thirsty stranger, not James.

trueFalse.statement: The Holy Spirit is called the Paraclete, or Advocate.
trueFalse.explanation: James explains that the Father gives another Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, to abide with believers.

trueFalse.statement: The world knows and receives the Holy Spirit.
trueFalse.explanation: The world cannot receive the Spirit because it neither sees it nor knows it. Only believers know it.

trueFalse.statement: The Holy Spirit teaches the believer about Jesus.
trueFalse.explanation: James says: the Holy Spirit teaches the believing one about Jesus.

trueFalse.statement: The stranger already knows Jesus when he arrives at the spring.
trueFalse.explanation: The stranger says: I do not know Jesus. He knows the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob but not Jesus.

trueFalse.statement: After drinking, the stranger sits under the tree with James and Salome.
trueFalse.explanation: After drinking, the stranger no longer stands but sits under the tree with James and Salome.

trueFalse.statement: James compares Jesus giving the water of life to Salome giving water to the stranger.
trueFalse.explanation: James says: just as Salome gives you water, so Jesus gives the water of life to the thirsty soul.

trueFalse.statement: The one who does not believe receives the Holy Spirit.
trueFalse.explanation: The one who does not believe does not receive the Spirit. The Spirit is given to the one who believes and seeks God.

trueFalse.statement: The Holy Spirit is sent by the Father in the name of Jesus.
trueFalse.explanation: This Spirit is sent by the Father in the name of Jesus to abide with believers forever.

trueFalse.statement: The Spirit speaks on its own authority, from itself.
trueFalse.explanation: The Spirit does not speak on its own; it speaks what it hears from Jesus.

trueFalse.statement: The Spirit bears witness about Jesus in the believing heart.
trueFalse.explanation: The Spirit bears witness about Jesus in the heart of the one who believes.

trueFalse.statement: The stranger asks no further questions and leaves immediately after hearing about the Spirit.
trueFalse.explanation: The stranger is silent and marvels, then rises and says he wants to hear more about this Spirit and what it does.

trueFalse.statement: The Holy Spirit helps believers remember the words of Jesus.
trueFalse.explanation: When a person does not remember the words of Jesus, the Spirit teaches again and brings the words back into his heart.

trueFalse.statement: James says that believers know the Holy Spirit because it abides with them and in them.
trueFalse.explanation: James says: we believers know it because it abides with us and is in us.

yesNo.question: Is the stranger thirsty when he comes to the spring?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The stranger says: I am very thirsty, I and my donkey.

yesNo.question: Does the stranger know the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The stranger says he knows the God who made heaven and earth, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.

yesNo.question: Does the world receive the Holy Spirit?
yesNo.explanation: No. The world cannot receive the Spirit because it neither sees it nor knows it.

yesNo.question: Does the Holy Spirit teach the believer about Jesus?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The Holy Spirit teaches the believing one about Jesus.

yesNo.question: Does the stranger marvel at what James says?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The stranger marvels and asks James: From where do you know these things? How do you know they are true?

yesNo.question: Does the one who does not believe receive the Holy Spirit?
yesNo.explanation: No. The one who does not believe does not receive the Spirit. It is given to the one who believes and seeks God.

yesNo.question: Does the Holy Spirit abide with believers forever?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The Father gives the Spirit so that it may abide with us forever, into the age.

yesNo.question: Does the Spirit speak from its own authority?
yesNo.explanation: No. The Spirit does not speak on its own but speaks what it hears from Jesus.

yesNo.question: Does the stranger want to hear more about the Holy Spirit?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. After being silent and marveling, the stranger rises and says: I want to hear more about this Spirit.

yesNo.question: Does the Spirit help believers who have forgotten the words of Jesus?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The Spirit teaches again and brings the words of Jesus back into the heart of the one who has forgotten.

yesNo.question: Can a woman who seeks God receive the Holy Spirit?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The woman who seeks God receives the Spirit just as the man does.
